title: safety-latch-controller-for-ab-experiments-with-synthetic-smoke-and-rollback-playbook
author: Priya Nair
description: Motivation: We need a predictable, safety-first controller for A/B experiments and small canaries that provides an automated fence (safety latch) when multiple safety signals correlate (latency spike, distribution drift, and negative quality regression). This PR implements an experimental Safety Latch Controller and an accompanying human-oriented rollback playbook. Design summary: 1) Safety Latch Controller: observes grouped signals (p50/p95 latency, tail latency counts, RU and token distribution drift via KL/JS divergence, user-visible error rate, and a lightweight model-quality delta computed from a rolling prompt set). The controller supports configurable conjunctive/threshold logic (e.g., two-of-three triggers) and emits annotated incidents and circuit states (OPEN/HELD/DRIVING) to the console and telemetry. 2) Synthetic Smoke Gate: before promoting traffic or increasing cohorts the controller can run a short synthetic smoke job that replays a small, representative prompt set against candidate model variants inside a shadow lane; metrics are collected and compared against baseline acceptance bands. 3) Human Latch Integration: when the controller enters HELD state the PR wires into the Console to surface an explicit "Human Latch" button with three canned actions (abort + rollback, hold for investigation, continue with manual OK). The API surface includes hooks for external on-call and SRE automation. 4) Rollback Playbook: a short, machine-readable playbook with steps and prefilled Linear/Jira templates for on-call to follow (investigate telemetry, gather smoke artifacts, execute rollback and run post-rollback sanity checks). Rollout plan: staged rollout for the feature itself (not a model rollout): start as a dry-run on canary lane in staging for 48 hours, then enable in prod default-off for 2 weeks with opt-in via route labels, then flip to default-on for selected tenants. Telemetry and metrics: new metrics prefixed safety_latch_* (trigger_count, state_transitions, synthetic_smoke_mismatch, avg_response_time_delta, drift_score) plus events in tracing (safety.latch.trigger). Backwards-compatible: controller respects existing rollout policies and only intercepts traffic when a policy explicitly opts-in by setting safeLatch: true. Why different from previous work: instead of a pure statistical gate or single-metric breaker this controller fuses multiple orthogonal signals and includes a synthetic smoke stage that exercises actual prompt-response quality. It provides an integrated human workflow so SREs and product owners can make informed decisions quickly. Checklist: - [x] Core controller logic and state machine implemented - [x] Synthetic smoke runner and comparator added - [x] Console UI hooks and latch API endpoints wired (UI skeleton only) - [x] Telemetry + metrics emitted and documented - [x] Unit and integration tests for state transitions (dry-run mode exercised) - [x] Playbook templates and Linear automation snippets included - [x] E2E in staging green (synthetic smoke + traffic simulation) Related work: ENG-2143 (experimentation platform enhancements), PRs touching rollout controller and telemetry (see changed files). Rollback story: when HELD triggers the controller will optionally run an automated rollback if configured in policy; otherwise it opens an incident and annotates the rollout with recommended rollback command and a link to a prefilled Linear card. See release_notes for operator-facing changes and the playbook for step-by-step guidance.

review_comments: Jakob Sorensen: Overall nice work. A few concerns: ensure the smoke runner intentionally limits cost and GPU time (we can't start big replays in prod). Can we make smoke job resource caps explicit in config?
Priya Nair (author): Addressed by adding smokeJob.maxTokens and smokeJob.maxDuration; default conservative caps set and documented in playbook.
Lina Chen: How do we avoid double-triggering when existing circuit-breakers already mark an unhealthy model? Seems we might generate duplicate incidents.
Priya Nair (author): SafetyLatch checks for existing circuit-breaker events and will dedupe; logic added to controller.go where we coalesce alerts by fingerprint and recent timestamp.

Marcus Hale: Tests look good, but add an integration test that simulates a noisy but non-correlated latency spike to ensure we don't get false positives. Also please add a prometheus-friendly metric for 'held_duration' so SREs can alert on prolonged holds.
Priya Nair (author): Added noisy-latency negative test and safety_latch_held_seconds metric; updated tests and docs.
Jakob Sorensen: CI flake on windows runner, reran and now green. Approving pending small doc tweak.
Lina Chen: Approving — good to land as experimental behind flag.
Marcus Hale: Approved. Recommend follow-up: UX polish for Console panel and adding RBAC check on the human-latch action in a later PR.
release_notes: Added experimental Safety Latch Controller (opt-in). New telemetry metrics safety_latch_trigger_count, safety_latch_state_transitions, safety_latch_held_seconds, and safety_latch_drift_score. Operator playbook available at redwood/docs/operator/playbooks/safety-latch-playbook.md. Default: feature disabled in prod; enable via rollout policy flag safeLatch: true. Note: synthetic smoke runner has conservative defaults to limit compute cost.
notes_for_operators: Playbook includes reproduction steps, smoke artifacts location, and prefilled Linear templates. On HELD state: check safety_latch.events, run smoke via console button, consider automatic rollback if configured. If opting for manual rollback run: `redwoodctl rollout rollback --rollout-id=<id> --reason='safety-latch-trigger'`. Contact SRE on-call if telemetry is inconclusive.
post_merge_actions: Enable experimental flag for staging canaries via config toggle: rollout.safety_latch.enabled = true
Monitor safety_latch_* metrics and adjust thresholds in the first 48h
Follow-up PR to add RBAC gate for human-latch actions
